sam: Ran an end-to-end nsys capture on ded-dev (A100), batch=8, seq=2048. Wanted a quick kernel-level sanity check. Command: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=run-1765123456 --sample=none ./serve --model redwood-v1 --bs 8 --seq 2048`
perf-bot: nsys HTML + timeline uploaded: s3://redwood-artifacts/perf/nsys/1765123456/index.html :white_check_mark:
sam: Quick top-line from the report (GPU active time slices collapsed):
  1) multi_head_attention_fwd_kernel —— 48.7% GPU time
  2) flash_attn_forward_kernel_v2 —— 19.2% GPU time
  3) kv_cache_read_kernel —— 8.4% GPU time
  4) fp16_matmul_128x64x8_kernel —— 6.9% GPU time
  5) softmax_reduce_kernel —— 4.1% GPU time
  6) cudaMemcpyAsync (H2D/D2H) —— 3.2% GPU time
  Others (launch overhead, small pointwise ops) —— rest
jess: Interesting. Do you have achieved occupancy / SM util counters for the top ones? flash vs mhattn often show different bottlenecks.
sam: Pulled SM counters from the nsys timeline: `multi_head_attention_fwd_kernel` SM_efficiency ~ 54%, Achieved_occupancy ~ 0.42; `flash_attn_forward_kernel_v2` SM_efficiency ~ 18%, Achieved_occupancy ~ 0.21. matmul kernel shows high instruction throughput but tensor core utilization low (~27%). KV read shows long serialization (many small memcpy/loads) causing warps to idle.
liam: That suggests two separate problems: mhattn is compute-heavy (good occupancy but suboptimal tensor core usage), flash_attn is launch/occupancy-starved. For flash: try increasing threads-per-block or batching multiple heads per block, or fallback to the alternate `flash_attn_legacy` that has higher occupancy for long seq.
maya: In the perfetto flame view I see repeated short gaps right before `kv_cache_read_kernel` where the stream waits on small cudaMemcpyAsync chunks (lots of tiny D2H/H2D). The decode loop is interleaving host copies and kernel launches. Screenshot in the trace: https://perfetto.app/trace/1765123456 (link)
sam: Actionable list I propose:
  - (liam) prototype increasing threads/block for `flash_attn_forward_kernel_v2` and test achieved_occupancy (A/B on dev pool)
  - (jess) add a KV prefetch coalescer to aggregate small fetches into larger batched loads, re-run nsys to measure reduction in memcpy stalls
  - (maya) capture perfetto with CPU scheduling + NVTX next run to confirm host-side stalls
  - (sam) test an alternate matmul kernel using fused int8 GEMM path to increase tensor core utilization
jess: Sounds good. Rough perf targets: reduce flash_attn GPU time by 2x (-> ~10%), reduce memcpy stalls from 3% to <1%, and lift tensor core util to >60% for matmul.
liam: I'll start with a param sweep for block/thread config tonight and run microbenchmarks. If occupancy goes up but SM_efficiency drops, we should look at register pressure/ILP.
maya: I'll schedule the perfetto capture and annotate NVTX ranges for decode and KV logic. Will post traces to the same S3 path.
sam: Cool — assign owners in the task board and re-run baseline capture after each change. Will also open a small perf regression issue if any change worsens end-to-end P95 latency. :eyes:
jess: Thanks team :thumbsup:
__notes: single Slack thread; messages are chronological and short-form per agents.md
